title: Every Screen Minute Needs a Job: The Pixel Budget Era
content:
Something changed in education forums this week — the question is no longer *whether* students use screens, but **what job each minute is doing**.

LAUSD and New York are publishing grade-by-grade screen budgets. Boston and Connecticut parent groups want one district rulebook: fewer solo devices in early years, carts instead of constant 1:1, and no screens as a reward for finishing lunch. Ed-tech threads say the same thing in vendor language — prove learning **and** prove the minute on glass is irreplaceable.

Teachers are tired of a different cost: AI suspicion without a playbook. Survey research this month describes "two-way suspicion" — hunches staff cannot prove and students cannot disprove — while forums keep returning to witnessed drafts, oral defenses, and clear use bands instead of detector scores.

India runs hotter on uncertainty: aspirants describe extended entrance cycles, sleep collapse, and mock whiplash after years of drops, even as CBSE improvement forms keep dinner tables on percentage panic.

EduHexa partners with 100+ institutions when leaders need **screen budgets, proof tasks, and parent language** aligned — not another tool rollout without a job description.

Does every digital task in your timetable say what offline alternative exists?
excerpt: LAUSD-style screen budgets, parent petitions, and AI suspicion are pushing schools to document what every digital minute does — and where witnessed proof replaces uploads.
